claim: The ULA transparency test covers the border: a border whose colour after the palette equals NextREG 0x14 is transparent and shows the layers below, and turning the ULA off (0x68 bit 7) still leaves it a blend source.
limit: Seen by eye on a KS1 (core 3.03.00, nxsuite V05 border, V04 rules); the blend-source part with the ULA off not measured.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 17
evidence.text: ULA, LoRes and Layer 2 are transparent by colour after the palette against NextREG 0x14; sprites and tilemap by index before the palette against 0x4B / 0x4C. The fallback colour 0x4A resets to E3, as 0x14 does.
KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite V05): Layer 2 showed through side borders in the $14 colour (operator answer lower-green).
KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite V04): ULA and Layer 2 were transparent by colour = $14, tilemap and sprites by index = $4C / $4B (operator).
